items.expected-result: `ai-raccoon repair project-ids` (no --map, dry run) completes well within the CLI's 100s HttpClient timeout against a real-shaped, real-size copy of the live production bank (53,207 entries, ~1.4GB, vec_entries/vec_structure populated at production scale) -- the exact symptom reported: "ai-raccoon: no settings server answered at http://127.0.0.1:7721/mcp (The request was canceled due to the configured HttpClient.Timeout of 100 seconds elapsing.)"
items.command: sqlite3 -readonly ~/.ai-raccoon/memory.db "VACUUM INTO '<scratch>/memory-copy.db'"; cleared watches/watch_files/watch_digest_claims on the copy; served it with this branch's fixed build on a scratch port (`AiRaccoon --data-root <scratch-data-root> serve --port 0 --idle-timeout 0`); `time AiRaccoon --data-root <scratch-data-root> --port <bound-port> repair project-ids`
items.evidence: real time 3.025s total (user 0.17s, sys 0.04s). Output: "project-ids repair: 47 id(s) censused -- 0 fold, 0 drop (test residue), 0 retire (registered, empty), 41 need a human to attribute, 6 need nothing (already correct or empty). Dry run -- pass --apply to run this." plus the full unattributed-id list and a written alias-map template -- a complete, correct report, not a partial/truncated one. Before this fix, the same query shape measured directly against this same live bank (via EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN + raw timing, recorded in the PR's planning record) cost 54.9-96.5s on the vec_entries leg alone and 14.4-41.9s on the vec_structure leg -- either alone exceeds the 100s client timeout; together with the census's other ~20 queries the reported failure is fully explained. This run exercises the exact fixed code path (ProjectIdCensus.CollectAsync via the real CLI -> HTTP -> RepairEndpoint -> SqliteRepairStore pipeline), at real production scale, end to end.
items.observed-result: the reported CLI-timeout symptom does not reproduce against the real bank once this fix is applied; report is fast and complete
